title: The Bird and the Girl
checkpoint: Year 1 Autumn 1, week 2 — School readiness — Phase 5: new sounds ea, oy, ir
note_for_grown_ups: A Phase 5 book for the new sound 'ir' — another way to write the /ur/ sound your child knows from 'turn', used in bird, girl and first.

pages.illustration: Pip drawn small and neat on a park railing, seen against a big open park background so his smallness reads. Fresh greens.

pages.text: Pip sees a girl in the park.
pages.illustration: A child sitting cross-legged on the grass a little way off, seen from Pip's low viewpoint so she seems large and gentle. Keep her generic and warm.

pages.text: The girl sits on the dirt.
pages.illustration: The child sitting on a bare patch of earth scratching a pattern in the dirt with a stick, absorbed. Pip watching from the railing.

pages.text: Pip is the first to hop up.
pages.illustration: Pip hopping down onto the grass — the brave first hop — one foot forward, wings half out, everything about him tentative.

pages.text: Olive is a big bird too.
pages.illustration: Olive the owl landing heavily on the railing behind Pip, huge by comparison, blocking out a chunk of sky. Comic size contrast.
Olive doing a slow showy turn on the railing with her wings out, half pirouette, entirely pleased with herself. Movement arc.

pages.text: The girl had fun with the birds.
pages.illustration: The child laughing with both birds near her — Pip on her knee, Olive on the railing. Warm, gentle, no touching of the owl.
The two birds flying away over the park treetops together, the child waving small below them. Aerial viewpoint.
Closing page: Pip and Olive back on their own branch in the oak at sunset, the park visible far off. Warm and homeward.
